authoring_review.review_type: Translation authoring and focused self-check; no independent reviewer or reader testing.

completed_work: Source-first connected narrative draft of all eight chapters, with verse-specific rationale and exact before/after/comparator/source hashes.
Selective notes and vocabulary preserve recurring biblical language and consequential textual choices.
Sentence boundaries cross verse labels where needed; the curse poem remains inside its verse paragraph.
All 46 cumulative ledger audits passed, including exact historical parent reads; all 186 new XML substrings are individually bound.
key_decisions: 1:8 retains the mouth image and unfolds spoken reflection on instruction; courage, rest and instruction connect with the Torah.
2 retains Rahab’s occupation, agency, life-for-life pledge, family rescue and the blood-on-heads responsibility image.
3:16 follows written at Adam and notes reading-tradition from Adam; 5:1 and 6:7 explicitly note consequential written/read alternatives.
4 retains both in-river and camp stones and repeated questions from children; ark of testimony is not renamed covenant.
5 preserves second-time circumcision and the ensuing generational explanation, narrator’s give us, and the commander’s abrupt No without supplying a doctrinal identity.
6 keeps herem’s dedication and destruction together, names victims, distinguishes treasury metals, and preserves the difficult warning of verse 18.
7 retains corporate indictment, full lineage, disputed Shebarim, man-by-man sequence, gold tongue image, children in the valley, and him/them punishment shift without inventing guilt.
8 retains thirty thousand and about five thousand, the north/west deployment and night notices, Bethel, men and women among twelve thousand dead, and sunset corpse removal.
8:30–35 closes the batch with instruction written and heard by the complete assembly, including women, children and resident foreigners.
remaining_review_questions: Independent Hebrew scholarship should assess difficult syntax at 3:16, 6:18, 7:17, 7:25 and 8:13–14,32.
The relation of the two troop counts and the night notices in Joshua 8 remains unresolved.
Names, terms and interpretive choices require whole-book consistency review after the remainder of Joshua is drafted.
Natural reading and listening goals have not yet been tested with readers; low overlap does not demonstrate comprehension or independent authorship.
overlap_qualification: Normalized whole-verse overlap is triage only, not fidelity, originality, comprehension or independent approval.
